The bell says every change: how it would read

Nothing in the app has changed. These are drawings for you to approve. Each “Today” picture is the real app as it is live now. Each “Every change” picture is the same bell with only the words of that line changed to say every change, its new words ringed in green. The pictures are at iPhone size unless they say otherwise. Tap any picture to enlarge it.

What to look at now: 13 questions

  1. A. Is this how the bell should read when it says every change?I recommend: Yes, as drawn. Nothing is cut off, but the longest line one save can make takes five rows on an iPhone, more than the three you were told.
  2. A2. Should the changes keep the order the bell uses today?I recommend: Yes. Whether it is still on, then when, then who, then what it is called, then the remark.
  3. A3. Should a changed remark still be said only as “remark changed”, without its new words?I recommend: Yes. A remark can be 200 letters; a tap opens the input to read it.
  4. A4. When three or more people are added, should the bell name them all, where it says “3 people added” today?I recommend: Name them all. It is the one count left in the line.
  5. A5. Should two names be joined with “and”, so they do not read as two separate changes?I recommend: Yes. “Sidewinder and Talisman added, Hex and Ace taken off”.
  6. A6. Should a phone message, once the app sends them, carry this same sentence?I recommend: Yes, word for word, so the bell and the phone never disagree.
  7. B. When a change is undone after Ranger’s phone was told of it, should his phone get a second message?I recommend: Yes. A message on a phone cannot be taken back, so the second one corrects it.
  8. C. A leave made another kind and a half day: “Now OL (AM), LL changed to OL”.I recommend: “Now AM, LL changed to OL”. The new kind is said once.
  9. D. A morning leave made a Training: “Now 00:00–12:00, LL changed to Training”.I recommend: “LL changed to Training, 00:00–12:00”. The times did not move; they are its hours now.
  10. E. A morning leave moved to another day says no “(AM)”: “Now Thu 6 Aug”.I recommend: “Now Thu 6 Aug (AM)”, as when a leave is moved and made a half day.
  11. F. A title given to an input that had none: “Renamed — was Training”.I recommend: Keep it. It was called Training and is now called Sim.
  12. G. A title taken away: “Renamed — was Brief”.I recommend: Keep it, for the same reason.
  13. H. An Attach sent somewhere else: “Renamed — was Exercise Kite · 145 Sqn”.I recommend: “145 Sqn changed to 146 Sqn”, like “LL changed to OL”.

Question A Is this how the bell should read when it says every change?

This happens whenever a scheduler changes an input someone is on: on the Inputs page or the schedule, Saber changes several things in one save, and each person on the input reads one line in the bell. How often a save changes three or more things is not counted by the app; my guess is that most saves change one or two.

Today
The bell says the first two changes, then how many more: “and 1 more change”. What the other changes were is not said.
Every change
Every change of that save is said, in the order the bell already uses, joined by commas, each after the first starting with a small letter unless it starts with a name. A replaced Leave War bid is still said last.
Longer than said
When you agreed, you were told a line might run to a third row on your iPhone. Drawn, five changes already take three rows, and the longest line one save can make takes five rows. On a desktop the bell is narrower than on a phone, so a line can take a row more there: the four changes take two rows on an iPhone and three rows on a desktop.
I recommend
Yes, as drawn. Nothing is cut off: the bell lets a line run to as many rows as it needs, and the list scrolls. A line of two changes reads exactly as today. My guess is that long lines are rare, and they are the saves where Ranger most needs to know what changed.

The longest line one save can make

Ranger, Hex and Ace are on a Training called “Advanced range safety procedures brief 1” (40 letters, the longest title the app takes) on Mon 27 Jul. In one save Saber makes it a course called “Range course”, runs it Tue 28 to Thu 30 Jul from 08:00 to 11:30, adds Sidewinder and Talisman, takes Hex and Ace off and changes its remark. A course files itself under Unavailable, so that is said too.

Today
“Filed under Unavailable, now Tue 28 Jul – Thu 30 Jul 08:00–11:30, and 5 more changes · Saber”, two rows
Every change
“Filed under Unavailable, now Tue 28 Jul – Thu 30 Jul 08:00–11:30, Sidewinder, Talisman added, Hex, Ace taken off, Training changed to CSE, renamed — was Advanced range safety procedures brief 1, remark changed · Saber”, five rows

The same line on a desktop (the bell is a little narrower there) and in the iPhone's own browser engine: five rows on the desktop, five rows on the iPhone engine.

Why no save can say more. One save can change, at most: whether it is on the programme or under Unavailable; its days and hours; who is added; who is taken off; its kind; its name; its remark. That is seven. Cancelling is an eighth, but no window that changes an input can cancel it in the same save: cancelling is a save of its own on the schedule. Ranger himself being added or taken off is never joined to the rest: he reads only “You were added” or “You were taken off”. So seven is the most, and this line is the longest the bell can show, apart from longer callsigns.

Question A2 Should the changes keep the order the bell uses today?

The same moment as question A: Ranger reads one line after Saber changed several things in one save.

The order
Cancelled or not; on the programme or under Unavailable; the days and hours; who was added; who was taken off; the kind; the name; the remark. Then a replaced Leave War bid.
Example
“Filed under Unavailable, now Tue 28 Jul – Thu 30 Jul 08:00–11:30, Sidewinder, Talisman added, Hex, Ace taken off, Training changed to CSE, renamed — was Advanced range safety procedures brief 1, remark changed · Saber” (the longest case above).
I recommend
Yes. It goes from what matters most to Ranger (is it still on, is it still when he thought) to what matters least. Today’s line already uses this order for its first two.

Question A3 Should a changed remark still be said only as “remark changed”, without its new words?

Saber changes the remark on Ranger’s Training from “Bring your kit” to “Bring water”, with or without other changes.

As drawn
“Now Tue 14 Jul, remark changed · Saber”.
The other way
“Now Tue 14 Jul, remark now Bring water · Saber”. A remark can be up to 200 letters, so one remark could fill the bell.
I recommend
Say “remark changed”. A tap on the line opens the input with its remark.

Question A4 When three or more people are added, should the bell name them all?

Saber adds Ace, Sidewinder and Talisman to Ranger’s Training in one save. Ranger is already on it.

Today
“3 people added · Saber”. One or two are named: “Ace added”, “Ace, Talisman added”. The same for people taken off.
Named
“Ace, Sidewinder and Talisman added · Saber”. Ten people would make a line of ten names.
I recommend
Name them all. “Say every change” leaves this as the one count in the line. No picture: the drawing copy changed only the “and 1 more change”, not this.

Question A5 Should two names be joined with “and”?

The longest case above: Saber adds two people and takes two off in one save.

As drawn
“Filed under Unavailable, now Tue 28 Jul – Thu 30 Jul 08:00–11:30, Sidewinder, Talisman added, Hex, Ace taken off, Training changed to CSE, renamed — was Advanced range safety procedures brief 1, remark changed · Saber”. The commas between names and the commas between changes look the same, so “Talisman added, Hex, Ace taken off” can read as three changes.
With “and”
“…, Sidewinder and Talisman added, Hex and Ace taken off, …”
I recommend
Yes. It changes only lines that name two or more people.

Question A6 Should a phone message carry this same sentence?

Once the app sends messages to phones (at the database step), Saber’s save would send Ranger a message as well as the bell line.

Example
The message would read: “Range course, Tue 28 Jul: Filed under Unavailable, now Tue 28 Jul – Thu 30 Jul 08:00–11:30, Sidewinder, Talisman added, Hex, Ace taken off, Training changed to CSE, renamed — was Advanced range safety procedures brief 1, remark changed · Saber”.
I recommend
Yes, word for word. There is no phone message to picture yet.

Question B When a change is undone after Ranger’s phone was told of it, should his phone get a second message?

This happens when a scheduler presses Undo after a save, for example to take back a slip. Saber moves Training from Wed 15 to Thu 16 Jul, and Ranger’s phone says so. Saber presses Undo. Ranger’s phone gets a second message that Training is back on Wed 15 Jul.

In the bell
This is already how the bell is being made to work: a line Ranger has read gets a new line saying what is true now; a line he has not read simply goes.
On a phone
A message on a phone cannot be taken back once sent. So the only way to put it right is a second message.
The question
You said an undone change should get a notification of its own. Is this what you meant: a second phone message, as in the example?
I recommend
Yes. The second message’s words would be drawn and put to you before it is built.

No picture: the app does not send phone messages yet.

The wordings the last round left for you

Question C A leave made another kind and a half day

Saber opens Ranger’s LL on Mon 3 Aug (a whole day) on the Inputs page, makes it an OL and the morning only, in one save, for example when a leave was booked as the wrong kind.

Today
“Now OL (AM), LL changed to OL · Saber”. The line says “OL” before it says the LL was changed to an OL.
Option 1
“Now AM, LL changed to OL · Saber”
Option 2
“LL changed to OL, now AM · Saber”
I recommend
Option 1. It keeps the bell’s order and says the new kind once, the way a titled input already reads “Now AM”.

Question D A morning leave made a Training

Ranger’s LL on Tue 4 Aug is the morning only. Saber makes it a Training. A Training has no half days, so it takes the morning’s hours, 00:00 to 12:00. My guess is that this is rare.

Today
“Now 00:00–12:00, LL changed to Training · Saber”. Nobody typed 00:00–12:00; those are the morning’s hours, which did not move.
Option 1
“LL changed to Training · Saber”
Option 2
“LL changed to Training, 00:00–12:00 · Saber”
I recommend
Option 2. Ranger learns his Training runs 00:00 to 12:00, which is likely a slip he can point out. It says the kind first, which differs from the bell’s order, so it is your call.

Question E A morning leave moved to another day

Ranger’s LL on Wed 5 Aug is the morning only. Saber moves it to Thu 6 Aug and leaves it the morning, for example when a leave is swapped to another day.

Today
“Now Thu 6 Aug · Saber”. The line does not say it is still the morning.
Option 1
“Now Thu 6 Aug (AM) · Saber”
Option 2
Leave it: the half did not change.
I recommend
Option 1. It reads like a leave moved and made a half day, “Now Thu 16 Jul (AM)”, which you approved.
